messages.author: 2857a36d0d07bb2f
messages.subject: Doesn't Recognize my .csv Files
parts:
Hello,

When I run GGIR I get this error 
"Checking that user has read access permission for all files in data directory: Yes
Checking that user has write access permission for directory specified by argument outputdir: Yes
Error in g.part1(datadir = datadir, outputdir = outputdir, f0 = f0, f1 = f1,  : 
  
No files to analyse. Check that there are accelerometer filesin the directory specified with argument datadir"

Here is the code I am running:


library(GGIR)
g.shell.GGIR(
  mode=c(1,2,5),
  datadir="H:/RData/NewData/",
  outputdir="H:/RData/OutputData",
  do.report=c(2,5), f0=0, f1=1,
  #=====================
  # Part 2
  #=====================
  strategy = 1,
  hrs.del.start = 0,          hrs.del.end = 0,
  maxdur = 9,                 includedaycrit = 16,
  qwindow=c(0,24),
  mvpathreshold =c(100),
  bout.metric = 4,
  excludefirstlast = FALSE,
  includenightcrit = 16,
  #=====================
  # Part 3 + 4
  #=====================
  #def.noc.sleep = 1,
  #outliers.only = TRUE,
  #criterror = 4,
  #do.visual = TRUE,
  #=====================
  # Part 5
  #=====================
  threshold.lig = c(30), threshold.mod = c(100),  threshold.vig = c(400),
  boutcriter = 0.8,      boutcriter.in = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
  boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in = c(1,10,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,10),
  boutdur.mvpa = c(1),
  #=====================
  # Visual report
  #=====================
  timewindow = c("WW"),
  visualreport=TRUE)

There are definitely the exported .csv files in the folder, so I am not sure where things seem to be going wrong. 

Thanks.
Alexa

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Doesn't Recognize my .csv Files
parts:
Do the files contain raw data?

GGIR in its current form cannot handle epoch aggregated data from ActiLife.
It is common for new GGIR users with Actigraph data to not realise that the data they exported is not the raw but the aggregated data.
A typical raw data file is at least 20 MB in size and for multi-day recordings even a lot larger.

Best, Vincent

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Doesn't Recognize my .csv Files
parts:
Hi Giulia,
Those recordings are probably too short for meaningful analysis with GGIR, you would have to change argument windowsizes to be able to process such a short file.
My advise is to look out for a multi-day recording. I think shared one in this google group before.

Other tips:
- If you have GENEActiv data focus on the bin file format it produces. GGIR is best test for these.
- check that you do not have any non-acceleromater csv files in the folder specified by datadir, GGIR is may be confused if it encounters other csv files that are not accelerometer data.
- set print.filename = TRUE and do.parallel=FALSE, in that way you can check that GGIR is trying to process the actual file you are interested in.
Vincent
